question: During laparoscopic tubal sterilization, the fallopian tube must be traced from its uterine cornual origin before a Filshie clip is applied, because the round ligament lies close to the tube at the cornu and its accidental ligation would constitute a failed sterilization without causing harm to the patient.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is accurate. The round ligament is the structure most often confused with the fallopian tube at the cornual region. Accidental round-ligament ligation results in a failed sterilization (the patient remains fertile) but no direct harm — except the consequence of an unintended pregnancy. Always trace from the cornua to the fimbriae.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The round ligament runs alongside the fallopian tube at the uterine cornu, and visually they can appear similar — especially under laparoscopic magnification in a narrow pelvis. Tracing the tube from the cornua distally to confirm its fimbriated end is the only reliable way to distinguish tube from round ligament before clip placement.
